title: Symphony Masala Brings Bollywood to American Orchestras for the First Time
excerpt: Indian-American conductor Roger Kalia and vocalist Anuradha Palakurthi have created the first-ever symphonic arrangements of Bollywood music for Western instruments, with sold-out performances from New Hampshire to Santa Monica.
body:
• Symphony Masala is the first-ever project to arrange Bollywood songs for a full Western symphony orchestra without Indian instruments
  • Created by Indian-American conductor Roger Kalia and vocalist Anuradha "Juju" Palakurthi, the show premiered in 2023 with Symphony New Hampshire
  • Performances with Orchestra Santa Monica in January 2026 sold out within three days of tickets going public
  • The Chicago Sinfonietta staged the Chicago premiere in October 2025, timed with Diwali

For decades, Bollywood music has been one of the world's most widely heard musical traditions, resonating with over two billion people globally. Yet until 2023, no one had arranged its iconic songs for a Western symphony orchestra. That changed with Symphony Masala, a collaboration between Indian-American conductor Roger Kalia and acclaimed Bollywood vocalist Anuradha "Juju" Palakurthi that is quietly rewriting the concert programming playbook in American orchestral halls.

From Pandemic Idea to Sold-Out Concerts

The project was conceived during the pandemic and debuted on October 21, 2023, at the Nashua Center for the Arts in New Hampshire as part of Symphony New Hampshire's centennial season. That performance brought together musicians from the United States and Mumbai to develop original symphonic scores for Bollywood songs — entirely without traditional Indian instruments.

"It was probably the first such concert in the United States. It was a dream to elevate Indian music onto the symphonic stage, and a true honor to debut it with the oldest professional orchestra in New Hampshire."

— Anuradha "Juju" Palakurthi, co-creator of Symphony Masala

The show features 15 songs spanning 70 years of Indian cinema, from the iconic theme from Sholay to "Chaiyya Chaiyya" from the 1998 film Dil Se to the Oscar-winning "Jai Ho" from Slumdog Millionaire. The arrangements preserve the microtonal vocal inflections central to Bollywood singing while placing them within a full Western symphonic framework.

A Concert That Sells Itself

Orchestra Santa Monica hosted Symphony Masala on January 10, 2026, at the Eli and Edythe Broad Stage at the Santa Monica College Performing Arts Center. The free concert sold out within three days of tickets becoming available — an unusual feat for a symphony event, as Violinist.com editor Laurie Niles noted in her review of the performance.

The show featured Palakurthi and co-vocalist Charenjeet "CJ" Virdi, with dancers from the Svetlana Tulasi Dance Company. Arrangers included D.J. Sparr and Bappa Lahiri.

Niles, a veteran orchestral musician who had never played Bollywood music in hundreds of pops concerts, described the experience of learning the repertoire as transformative. "Once I could sing them a few times, they came easily to my fingers, and I found my brain wanted to keep repeating them — like taking more bites of a yummy new kind of food," she wrote.

Chicago and Beyond

The Chicago Sinfonietta staged the Chicago premiere in October 2025, with performances at Wentz Concert Hall in Naperville and the Studebaker Theater in Chicago. Kalia, a former Freeman Conducting Fellow with the Sinfonietta, led the performances timed to coincide with Diwali. The Indian Eye, a national South Asian publication, featured the concerts as a milestone in cross-cultural orchestral programming.

Kalia currently serves as Music Director of the Evansville Philharmonic and Orchestra Santa Monica, and was recently appointed Music Director of the Terre Haute Symphony Orchestra. He has received multiple awards from the Solti Foundation and has been profiled by Symphony Magazine for his innovative programming.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian Americans and the broader diaspora, Symphony Masala represents something rare: Indian cultural expression presented not as exotic novelty but as a natural extension of the Western classical tradition. The project bridges two musical worlds that have historically operated in parallel, offering diaspora audiences the chance to hear the songs of their childhood performed with the institutional weight of a full symphony orchestra.

As Palakurthi told Orchestra Santa Monica: "Bollywood music resonates with over two billion people around the world, and many of these melodies are considered among the greatest ever written. By reimagining them with full symphonic orchestration, we're able to present them on a truly global stage."

What's Next

Kalia's upcoming guest engagements include a debut with the Canton Symphony Orchestra and a return to the Redlands Symphony. Symphony Masala appears positioned for further expansion as more American orchestras seek programming that reflects the diversity of their communities. The Evansville Philharmonic's current season and future dates for the project have not yet been announced.
